title: The Hypocrisy of Science-Based Lifters
summary: An open letter of 10 questions to science-based fitness influencers, prompted by Jeff Nippard's self-critical video. NH argues that the criticism targets the influencers' attitude and methods, not science. He calls science-based content a cult-like, unaccountable gimmick that fuels optimization anxiety in novices, tolerates PED users and oversells inconclusive studies.
claims: Jeff Nippard's video criticizing his own science-based approach is commendable because self-criticism is rare on fitness YouTube, but it left out the influencers' attitude and methods
Almost nobody opposes the scientific method; critics attack the influencers' interpretation and character, so calling them anti-science is a dishonest shield and self-victimization
Many science-based influencers start from an emotionally charged preference, cherry-pick studies to justify it and ignore contrary evidence, which is itself anti-scientific
For most creators science-based is a profitable gimmick: few have scientific credentials, at best they are middlemen, and many misread studies that say the opposite of their claims
The evidence-based label grants instant credibility and escapes the source and credential demands placed on experience-based lifters; it should get extra scrutiny instead
Maybe 1 in 100 viewers reads the cited studies, so the whole system runs on trust, the enemy of science, and the top influencers act like prophets or cult leaders
The fastest way to grow in science-based circles is to flatter a bigger creator for shout-outs, much like kissing the don's ring in a mafia
He polices natural lifters in his own community when they spread harmful content; science-based creators rarely police their own
Non-lifters now enter the community by claiming to be science-based; he holds that you cannot be a good fitness educator without lifting yourself
Science-based influencers rarely apologize for promoting bad studies; they swap in a new study and blame the literature, although they chose and interpreted it
Holding influencers to a high standard of honesty protects information quality; experience-based coaches must swallow their pride and apologize when wrong
The science-based community is intolerant of criticism; fans, especially Mike Israetel's, are dogmatic and aggressive, and the leaders do not correct it
The divide between science-based lifters and mindless just-lift people is largely fabricated; people tracked their weights 100 years ago and even the most bro lifter knows his bench numbers
Experience-based lifters also build a strawman of tiny science-based lifters with pink dumbbells; most people, and the best approach, sit in the middle between experience and science
Science-based content sells a philosophy and an identity more than a training method
His own focus on optimizing for hypertrophy comes from years of strength training that he was told would bring size and brought only injuries and fat
Optimization content plays on fear of missing out; about 90% of the audience are novices, and optimizing is the surest way for a novice to stay a novice; they should try things and see what works
The mindset built by simply training is what got experienced lifters where they are; refinement and optimization come after
Promising 30-40% more growth from each new method keeps viewers in an endless loop of hesitation and program-hopping, like a dog chasing a car
Perfect is the enemy of good
Optimizing minor training details makes no sense for PED users whose drugs dwarf those effects; Mike Israetel being enhanced and coaching enhanced people makes his methods dubious

In his gym he meets naturals doing slow-tempo lateral raises with 10 lb, not progressively overloading or going to failure, which are the cornerstone of building muscle, because of science-based content
Many people would have had healthier training if they had never found science-based content

Most supposed breakthroughs have been in the literature for about 30 years, while newer studies on volume, tempo, partials and lengthened training are inconclusive and contradict each other, which keeps the content flowing
Science-based content is popularization made for entertainment; like pop philosophy, it removes the work of reaching your own conclusions
Processed fitness science is like Kellogg's to oatmeal: tastier and easier but much less healthy
Science-based content became a social media phenomenon roughly 15 years ago
